experiment_data.hypothesis: Fine-tuning on depth-0 (original) text produces lower held-out perplexity than fine-tuning on higher-depth (recursive) text, because d0 data has higher quality signal without recursive degradation artifacts.
experiment_data.notes: Hypothesis "d0_only has lowest PPL" NOT supported. d1_only (5.55) and mixed_all (5.55) tied for best, both beat baseline (5.67) and d0_only (5.65). Surprising: first-generation (d1) text is better training data than human (d0). Reframing: depth estimation enables non-trivial data curation—optimal depth is d1, not d0. 500 samples/subset, Pythia-410M LoRA, held-out PPL eval.
